title: Snack benchlet notes — compact run tracker
body:
Purpose: tiny personal tracker for quick A/B micro-bench runs — keep things snack-sized so I actually record them. Use this to decide which configs to escalate to the shared bench dashboard.

Quick goals (today):
- sanity check 4-bit quantized variant on short-seq chat workload (max seq 512).
- find batch sweet spot for sub-50ms tail for 1–2 token generation.
- capture cost-per-1k tokens (rough) to compare to baseline.

Run table (manual capture, median over 10 samples unless noted):

| run | model | quant | batch | seq_max | p50_lat_ms | p95_lat_ms | cost_per_1k | success% | notes |
|-----|-------|-------|-------|---------|------------:|------------:|------------:|---------|-------|
| R1  | llama-2-13b | fp16  | 1     | 64      | 28          | 55          | $0.60      | 100     | baseline host api (dev region) |
| R2  | llama-2-13b | int4  | 1     | 64      | 18          | 38          | $0.22      | 98      | slight decoding variance, one mismatch in tokenization |
| R3  | llama-2-13b | int4  | 4     | 64      | 35          | 80          | $0.08      | 100     | batching helps cost but p95 spikes > SLO |
| R4  | redwood-vicuna-7b | fp16  | 2     | 128     | 22          | 48          | $0.18      | 100     | similar quality, cheaper absolute cost |
| R5  | redwood-vicuna-7b | int8  | 2     | 128     | 19          | 45          | $0.12      | 99      | quality check pass on small prompt set |
| R6  | llama-2-13b | int4  + kvcache | 1 | 512 | 42 | 70 | $0.20 | 97 | long context increases p50/p95 as expected; needs warm cache test |

Quick takeaways:
- int4 gives large cost wins with mild latency benefit for single-token generation; model-specific quirks (tokenization) caused one small mismatch (R2).
- batching (R3) reduces unit cost but pushes p95 beyond our 75ms soft target for short-turn chat — not good for low-latency UX without smarter batching windows.
- smaller model (redwood-vicuna-7b) is worth considering for price-sensitive endpoints; quality still acceptable for our micro-eval set.
- long context runs show expected cache warm-up behavior; need controlled warm-cache runs to measure steady-state.

Open questions / micro experiments to run next:
- Warm-cache steady state test: run R6 variant with 50 warmup requests before measuring.
- Explore dynamic batching window of 15ms to see p95 tradeoff (simulate at throughput ~50rps).
- Run token-level quality diff on R2 vs baseline for the 20 hardest prompts from customer set.
- Try per-route routing to vicuna for non-critical routes (savings calc).

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Add R2/R5 flagged prompts to small eval suite and push to CI (linked artifact: GH PR above).
- [ ] Re-run R3 with adaptive batch-size logic (simulate delays).
- [ ] Share summary in #applied-ml with key stats and ask SRE about enabling warm-cache flag on dev pool.

Notes to self: keep these snack summaries under 1 screen. If a run looks promising, make a full notebook and move to shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/bench-notebooks.

End of sheet.
